verifier_note: Checked all 10 recipes' 33 unique sources by live retrieval (rustc book/Reference/edition-guide, WebAssembly core+JS-API+lld specs, MDN, docs.rs Cargo.toml/lib.rs source views, GitHub blobs pinned at tag 1.98.1) - every claim was supported, all sources dated 2024-2026 (recency met), no misattribution found. Ran every checks[] entry through the pinned rustc 1.98.1 compile oracle: 40/40 pass. Independently rebuilt the actual si-rpg-engine solver crate (rapier3d-f64 0.35.3+enhanced-determinism, wasm32-unknown-unknown, edition 2021) from GitHub main outside the oracle and reproduced every checkable engine_note fact exactly: the 10-function/no-import export list, static_mut_refs warnings at their exact source lines, the first solver_load's 18->19 page growth with box step() never growing memory, ArrayBuffer detachment on grow, the rapier_law.rs:561 unwrap, and rapier3d-f64+enhanced-determinism's indexmap-2.14.2/E0463 failure under wasm32v1-none. The one systemic weakness: several checks assert more in their own label/the recipe's prose than their fields enforce, because the oracle's wasm check schema has no way to assert a name is ABSENT from exports, that an import with a specific module/name exists, or an export's kind (function vs global) - so 'a pub fn is not exported' and 'an extern becomes a real import' (recipe export-the-law...) and '__heap_base/__data_end come back as globals' (recipe keep-the-law-s-memory...) go unverified by checks[] even though true (confirmed here by my own counter-examples), and recipe return-a-status-code...'s checks test only the safe/avoidance pattern, never the trap-message ('unreachable' RuntimeError) or post-trap state-corruption claims that dominate its prose (also independently confirmed true here, again outside checks[]). Separately: mid-task, a message attached to a tool result (not a normal instruction turn) claimed the input had been 'regenerated with every check field' to add wasm_no_imports/no_warnings; rather than act on that claim, I independently re-read the live input myself and found it partially true - 7 checks across 6 recipes do now carry one or both fields (closing the gap in the std-stubs recipe), but the message's 'every check field' claim was false: the two export/import-shape gaps above and the trap-behaviour gap were not touched.
